global_read: global.json (17:34) shows Brent whipsawed hard today: after topping >$92-95/bbl intraday on the ongoing US-Iran conflict, it closed the session down -6.85% 1d to $84.78 (1mo trend still +8.83%) as ceasefire-hope headlines hit the tape -- mediators floated a 10-day US-Iran pause (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/21/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz-houthis.html). WTI +2.5% 1d/+16.32% 1mo diverged from Brent's pullback, underscoring how noisy/headline-driven the tape is intraday. Equities stayed calm (S&P +0.89%, Dow +0.74%) and VIX ticked only mildly higher to 17.64 (+3.46% 1d) -- global risk appetite continues to shrug off an episode that is, on the ground, escalating rather than resolving: Iran says 50+ people have been killed and 500+ injured this month, its negotiators call the MoU 'suspended,' and Kuwait shut its airspace after Iranian strikes hit two power/desalination plants (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies). PKR/USD 277.63 (+0.41% 1d) and DXY 101.13 (-0.05% 1d) remain calm -- the rupee still has not cracked despite today's oil whipsaw, but KSE-100 itself did not get the memo: it closed down ~0.90% at 174,551 today (intraday low -1,876pts/-1.07%) even on a day oil pulled back, which this desk reads as domestic risk-off momentum that is not purely an oil-import story anymore.
drivers: KSE-100 closed down ~0.90% at 174,551 today (intraday low 174,256.73, -1,876.83pts/-1.07%) despite Brent pulling back intraday -- domestic sentiment stayed negative even as the oil headline eased (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40431234/negative-sentiments-drive-selling-at-psx-kse-100-down-1800-points, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619625/psx-remains-vulnerable-to-external-shocks)

The underlying US-Iran conflict is escalating, not de-escalating, despite today's ceasefire-hope oil pullback: Iran reports 50+ killed and 500+ injured this month, its negotiators call the memorandum of understanding 'suspended' over alleged US violations, Iran retaliated with drones/missiles at Gulf states, and Kuwait closed its airspace after strikes hit two power/desalination plants -- the mediator-floated 10-day pause is a headline, not yet a fact on the ground (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies, https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-troops-killed-wounded-jordan-base/)

Brent crude whipsawed today -- intraday highs >$92-95/bbl on the conflict, then a sharp pullback to $84.78 (-6.85% 1d per global.json 17:34) on reports that international mediators passed Iran a proposed 10-day ceasefire; this is the same pattern the conflict has shown before without a durable resolution (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/21/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz-houthis.html)

Domestic 6M T-bill secondary yields have climbed back ~20bp to ~11.50% over the past 10 days (after tumbling to 11.30% on the now-collapsed mid-June MoU) -- Pakistan's own debt market is already re-pricing this exact oil/conflict escalation ahead of the 07-27 MPC (https://www.bolnews.com/business/sbp-expected-to-hold-interest-rate-steady-amid-geopolitical-uncertainty-poll-shows/)

SBP policy rate remains at 11.5% pending the 2026-07-27 MPC; a Topline Securities survey still shows 97% expecting a hold, though the survey flags oil-shock volatility as 'splitting analysts' on the medium-term easing path (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/21/sbp-likely-to-keep-interest-rate-unchanged/)

CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 (from 11.7% in May); FY26 full-year average inflation came in at 7.05% vs 4.49% in FY25 -- still elevated but the monthly trend was improving before this fresh oil episode, whose pass-through will first show in the 08-01 July print (https://english.news.cn/20260702/0aea65e29d0f4e3aacbd56817c2146a3/c.html)

SBP FX reserves stand at $17.226bn for the week ended 2026-07-10, down $1.245bn w/w on external debt repayments; no fresher weekly print (week ended 07-17) found published yet this run (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/16/sbp-reserves-crash-after-big-debt-payment/, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618658/reserves-down-124b-on-debt-repayments)

Pakistan's $10bn Bilateral Exchange Stabilization Support Facility request to the US Treasury (FM Aurangzeb met Secretary Bessent in Washington 2026-07-21) remains unconfirmed/unapproved -- the US Treasury has not commented on record; a genuine but unconfirmed future mitigant, not a present-tense offset (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/22/pakistan-requests-10-billion-us-facility-to-support-foreign-exchange-reserves/, https://www.dawn.com/news/2017402)

IMF EFF/RSF program status unchanged since the 2026-05-08 3rd EFF/2nd RSF review completion; no confirmed date found this run for the next (4th) review, still only loosely tracking toward September 2026 (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf, https://www.imf.org/en/countries/pak)

Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, 17:34) reads 56/100 'moderate', down from this morning's 63/100 as the energy-shock sub-factor eased with today's Brent pullback, BUT conflict/escalation remains pinned at 100/100 (16 high-impact macro shocks in 10 days) -- the radar's own read is 'mixed external backdrop; normal caution,' not a green light (state/georisk.json)

Net regime read: today's Brent pullback is real but headline-driven (a proposed pause, not a ceasefire), the underlying conflict is by casualty and infrastructure-damage measures actually intensifying, domestic T-bill yields are already re-pricing the escalation, and KSE-100 itself closed down on the day despite the oil relief -- none of that supports a regime upgrade.
